claims.text: A StatelessWidget builds only from its configuration (constructor inputs); its displayed content changes only when its parent rebuilds it with new inputs.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: StatelessWidget; refs/flutter-website ui/interactivity

claims.text: Widgets are immutable and recreated when their parent builds; a StatefulWidget's State object is created once (createState), persists while the widget stays in the tree, and has the build method.
DonHangApp extends StatelessWidget, has no fields, and its build returns the same MaterialApp every time.

ProductListScreen extends StatefulWidget with a final apiClient field and createState returning _ProductListScreenState, which holds late Future<List<Product>> _products set in initState from widget.apiClient.fetchProducts().
initState is called once, when the State object is inserted into the tree.
Inside a State, widget refers to the current widget object and gives access to its inputs.
The refresh button's _reload replaces _products with a new fetch inside the State.
LoginScreen's State holds text controllers, _error and _loading; CreateOrderScreen's State holds _result and _loading.
Use a StatefulWidget only when the widget must remember or change something by itself.

self_check.notes: Outline retargeted to stage-1 (DECISIONS.md §3): ProductListScreen is stateful because of _products, not a selected product. initState named in one sentence only; no other lifecycle methods, per depth_notes. setState left to the next lesson.
